spec.scope: In scope: item 1 (alert writer must not die silently), item 3 (fail-loud startup, compose healthcheck, CLAUDE.md text), item 4 (document alert drop, rate-limit queue-full warning). Item 2 does not exist in this task. Hard constraint: no git command that commits, pushes, stashes, restores, resets or otherwise changes history or discards working-tree changes; do not edit .claude/team/*/baseline* ; run pytest as `python -X faulthandler -m pytest -o faulthandler_timeout=120`; stop any python started.
spec.user_stories: - As an operator, a single malformed alert never stops all later alerts from being stored. - As an operator, if Postgres is unreachable or its startup load fails, the app refuses to start with a clear error instead of running with an empty watchlist and rule set. - As an operator, `docker compose up` still works because the backend waits until Postgres accepts connections. - As an operator, a burst of dropped alerts produces one summarised warning, not thousands of log lines, and the code states that alerts failing after the per-row retry are dropped.

design.item: - The writer loop must survive any non-cancellation exception. Wrap the whole iteration body (batch dequeue through backoff decision) so that `except asyncio.CancelledError: raise` and `except Exception: log.exception(...)` are the only outcomes; the loop then continues (short sleep of ALERT_FAILURE_BACKOFF_SECONDS after an unexpected error so a persistent fault cannot spin). - Row building is done per alert: an alert whose row cannot be built is logged with log.exception and dropped; the other alerts in the same batch are still written. (Needed because the item-1 test enqueues the bad and valid alert together and they land in one batch.) - task_done accounting: after the first blocking `get()` returns, exactly one task_done per alert actually dequeued (len(batch)), in a finally that also covers a failure during the further get_nowait() calls (count only what was dequeued). Queue.join() in _drain_alerts must therefore return after a bad batch. - Readability: replace the set-then-reset `failed` flag with `failed = row_failures > 0` computed after the row-by-row retry (failed is False when the batch insert succeeded). Behaviour of the existing backoff tests is unchanged.

- Database.connect() keeps its current contract (never raises; on any failure logs, closes the pool, `available` becomes False) so test_unavailable_database_raises keeps passing. Fail-loud is decided by Services. - db._backfill_watchlist: remove its inner try/except so a backfill failure propagates to connect()'s existing except (logs, pool closed, available False). Its early return for no pool / persist_rules False stays. - rules.RuleStore.load: stop swallowing; a failing repo.load_rules() propagates (class docstring updated). - main.Services.startup: after `await self.db.connect()`, if settings.rules_persistence_enabled is True: * if not self.db.available -> log.error with a clear line (Postgres unreachable / DATABASE_URL empty or wrong; no password or URL in the line) and raise RuntimeError; * `await self.rule_store.load()` and `await self.db.load_watchlist()` are no longer wrapped in swallowing try blocks; if either raises, log.error ("startup failed: loading rules/watchlist: ") and re-raise. On any startup failure Services.startup first awaits self.db.close() (workers, pool) and does not start the upstream; the lifespan exception propagates so uvicorn exits non-zero. The upstream factory/start only runs after the DB steps succeed. - Flags (choice, not removed): RULES_PERSISTENCE_ENABLED=true (default) means "Postgres is required": all the fail-loud checks above apply, and an empty DATABASE_URL counts as unreachable. RULES_PERSISTENCE_ENABLED=false is the explicit opt-out: startup skips rule/watchlist loading and the availability check, starts with empty rule store and watchlist, and rule/alert endpoints keep returning 503 (existing _require_rules_pool behaviour). TICKS_PERSISTENCE_ENABLED is unchanged: it only governs the tick writer task and never causes startup failure. Justification: the flag already means "rules go to Postgres", so true must mean required (invariant 5) and false is the only honest way to say "run without it". - docker-compose.yml: postgres gets healthcheck test `pg_isready -U ${POSTGRES_USER:-postgres} -d ${POSTGRES_DB:-ticks}` (CMD-SHELL) with interval, timeout, retries and start_period; backend `depends_on: postgres: condition: service_healthy`. frontend's depends_on and everything else untouched. - CLAUDE.md: remove "(fail-loud startup is not done yet)" in the project paragraph and say startup fails if Postgres is unreachable or its load fails and that RULES_PERSISTENCE_ENABLED=false is the opt-out; update invariant 5 wording if needed; mention the compose healthcheck; delete known issues 4, 5 and 6 (and the `failed` nit in 8) and fix the "Alert writer" paragraph (rate-limited warning, drop-after-retry documented, writer survives unexpected errors). The orchestrator reviews this text.

- At the point where alerts failing the per-row retry are dropped (the `if row_failures` branch), add a short comment: these alerts are intentionally dropped, not requeued (an outage must not grow memory or block ingestion). - New module constant ALERT_DROP_WARN_INTERVAL_SECONDS (e.g. 10.0) next to the other ALERT_* constants; no setting. Database keeps a drop counter and a monotonic timestamp of the last warning. In enqueue_alert's QueueFull branch: increment the counter; if no warning has been emitted yet or the interval has elapsed, emit ONE log.warning containing the text "alert queue full" and the number of alerts dropped since the last warning, then reset the counter. Still put_nowait only; never blocks, never raises. Known accepted limit: drops after the last warning of a burst are reported at the next drop.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Writer survives a bad alert. How to test (backend/tests/test_watchlist_alerts.py, using _db_with_stub/StubPool): enqueue an object whose row building raises (e.g. a stand-in missing `.threshold`, put straight on db._alert_queue or via enqueue_alert) and then a valid Alert before the writer runs, let the loop run, assert the valid alert is in pool.rows, db._alert_worker.done() is False, and `await asyncio.wait_for(db._alert_queue.join(), 1)` returns. MUST be run and recorded as FAILING against the current db.py before any change (current code: writer task ends with AttributeError, valid row never written, join hangs).

Unexpected non-batch exception does not kill the writer. Test: a stub pool whose acquire() raises something outside the inner except path is already covered by existing failure tests; add a second test where a bad alert alone is queued, then a valid one later (separate batches); valid one is written, task alive, log.exception record present (caplog).
Cancellation still works: existing test_close_during_backoff_is_not_delayed, test_close_is_bounded_when_write_blocks and the backoff/successful-write tests pass unchanged.

Fail-loud, DB down. Test: create_app(settings, upstream_factory=..., db=FakeDatabase(failing=True)) with default settings (rules_persistence_enabled True) -> entering TestClient raises (pytest.raises RuntimeError), an ERROR record is logged, FakeFinnhubClient.instances is empty or never started, and db.close was awaited.

Fail-loud, load failure. Tests: a fake DB that is available but whose load_rules raises, and one whose load_watchlist raises -> startup raises; RuleStore.load propagates a repo error (replaces the "swallows errors" test).

Fail-loud, real Postgres (test_rules_postgres.py, needs TEST_DATABASE_URL): (a) create_app with an unreachable URL (postgresql://u:p@127.0.0.1:1/none) -> TestClient entry raises; (b) with the real DB, a backfill failure makes Database.connect leave available False (e.g. alert_rules table whose symbol column breaks the backfill statement, or monkeypatching the backfill's statement execution to raise) and startup raises. Existing happy-path restart/round-trip tests pass.

Opt-out. Test: Settings(rules_persistence_enabled=False, database_url="") with the real Database starts (health 200), watchlist empty, rule and alert endpoints return 503. Fixture client_no_db becomes this configuration and test_api_rules / test_list_alerts_503 keep passing.
Runtime outage unchanged. Tests that flip fake_db.failing = True after a successful start (test_api_rules lines ~43/83/89, test_watchlist_alerts line ~74) still pass: 503, ingestion continues.

Compose. If docker is available, `docker compose config` validates and shows postgres healthcheck and backend `condition: service_healthy`; otherwise state docker was unavailable and check the YAML by reading. Only those two blocks changed in docker-compose.yml.
Drop comment present at the row-failure drop point in _alert_writer (review check).

Rate-limited warning. Test (extends test_alert_queue_full_drops_with_warning, queue size 1, no worker): enqueue 1 + N (e.g. 50) alerts in a burst with the clock frozen/monkeypatched -> exactly one "alert queue full" WARNING record from app.db, containing the drop count (1 for the first warning); advance the monkeypatched clock past ALERT_DROP_WARN_INTERVAL_SECONDS, drop again -> a second single warning whose count equals the drops since the first. enqueue_alert never raises and the queue size stays 1. The old substring "alert queue full" is kept.

Whole suite: offline `pytest` passes; with TEST_DATABASE_URL pointing at a throwaway PG17 cluster (initdb trust auth, temp dir outside the repo, port not 55432/55440/55461/55477) the real-Postgres tests pass with 0 skipped; any python/postgres process started is stopped afterwards.

spec.existing_tests_that_must_change: - backend/tests/conftest.py client_no_db: real Database with empty URL would now fail startup; build Settings(_env_file=None, finnhub_api_key="", database_url="", rules_persistence_enabled=False). Used by test_api_rules.py (test_no_db_rules_503..., test_503_body_leaks_nothing) and test_watchlist_alerts.py test_list_alerts_503; assertions stay. - backend/tests/test_api_symbols.py test_single_upstream_started_and_stopped_once: uses `settings` with the default real Database and empty URL, which now fails startup; pass db=FakeDatabase() (or the fake_db fixture). - backend/tests/test_watchlist_alerts.py test_startup_db_down_empty_watchlist_health_ok: asserts the old start-with-empty-watchlist behaviour; replace with fail-loud tests (criteria 4, 5, 7). - backend/tests/test_rules_engine.py test_store_load_swallows_errors_and_does_not_persist: RuleStore.load now propagates; rename and assert it raises, keeping the "store stays empty, put/discard never persist" assertions. - Unaffected (verified): test_rules_postgres.py test_unavailable_database_raises (connect still does not raise), the real-DB _app() tests, test_app_logger_info_and_idempotent_handlers (create_app() does not run lifespan), all tests using FakeDatabase() with default Settings.
spec.assumptions: - Ambiguity: the request says "Postgres unreachable" but an empty DATABASE_URL with the flag true is also treated as unreachable (fail), since the default flag value means Postgres is required. Chosen over silently allowing it, which would defeat fail-loud. - Ambiguity: "keep the valid alert written" when bad and valid share a batch is satisfied by per-alert row building, not by dropping the whole batch. - Flag semantics as in design: RULES_PERSISTENCE_ENABLED=false is the opt-out; TICKS_PERSISTENCE_ENABLED does not affect startup. No new settings; .env.example unchanged (optionally a one-line comment on the flag). - Services.startup, not Database.connect, raises, so connect()'s non-raising contract and its tests stay. - CLAUDE.md on disk has a "Known open issues" section (items 4, 5, 6 resolved by this task); the system-provided copy lacks it, the file on disk is the one to edit.
spec.edge_cases: - Bad alert is the first, last, or only item of a batch; batch of 200 with one bad row. - Batch dequeue interrupted by cancellation mid-fill: cancellation propagates, task_done counts match items dequeued. - Persistent unexpected writer fault must not busy-loop (backoff sleep). - Startup failure after the pool and workers were created (backfill or load failure): pool and worker tasks closed, no leaked tasks or connections. - Error log lines must not contain the DATABASE_URL or password. - Warning rate limit: first drop warns immediately; counter resets after each warning; a quiet period then a new drop warns again.

risks.risk: Making the default configuration require Postgres changes developer behaviour (uvicorn without a DB now exits); intended, but CLAUDE.md and the compose healthcheck must land together.
Rewriting _alert_writer's try structure could regress task_done accounting and hang Database.close(); covered by criteria 1 and 3.
The item-1 test constructs a bad alert object; if it fails for the wrong reason on current code the "fails before fix" proof is weak. Record the actual failure (writer task done, valid row missing).
Healthcheck uses env interpolation; a custom POSTGRES_USER/DB must match, hence the same defaults as the service.

spec.dependencies: asyncpg and pytest already pinned; no new packages. Files: backend/app/db.py, main.py, rules.py, docker-compose.yml, CLAUDE.md, backend/tests/{conftest.py,test_api_symbols.py,test_watchlist_alerts.py,test_rules_engine.py,test_rules_postgres.py,test_api_rules.py}, tests/fakes/fake_db.py (may need a way to make load_rules/load_watchlist raise while available). PostgreSQL 17 binaries for the real-DB run; docker optional.
spec.out_of_scope: Upstream call timeouts (issue 3), reconnect edge cases (issues 1-2), other test gaps (issue 7), frontend, revised-planning.md (orchestrator edits it), new settings, removing the persistence flags, requeueing or persisting dropped alerts, retrying the DB connection at startup, any git change.
spec.self_critique: Every story maps to criteria (1-3 writer, 4-9 startup/compose, 10-11 drop handling). Each criterion names a test or check. Biggest uncertainty: the flag choice (empty URL with flag true now fails) and whether the user expected it; flagged under assumptions. Second: criterion 6b needs an inventive way to force a backfill failure on a real DB; the implementer may use monkeypatching instead.
